questions.q: Using the same $f$ and $g$ as the previous question, find $(g\circ f)(x)$ and state its domain.
Verify that $f(x)=5x+1$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{5}$ are inverses by showing $f(g(x))=x$.
Does $f(x)=x^2$ (for all real $x$) have an inverse function? Explain.
questions.answer: No. $f$ is not one-to-one — it fails the horizontal line test, since for example $f(2)=f(-2)=4$. An inverse function only exists if the domain is restricted (e.g. to $x\geq0$).

sections.heading: Exponential equations and logs as inverses

questions.q: Solve $e^{2x-1}=20$, giving your answer to three decimal places.
The functions $f(x)=\log_3x$ and $g(x)=3^x$ are inverses. Use this fact to solve $3^x=81$ without a calculator, and state the value of $g(f(16))$.
The graph shows $f(x)=x^2$ (teal) and $g(x)=(x-2)^2+1$ (indigo). Describe the transformation that maps $f$ onto $g$.
questions.answer: $g$ is $f$ shifted right $2$ units and up $1$ unit — a horizontal translation of $+2$ followed by a vertical translation of $+1$.

questions.q: If $h(x)=-f(x+3)$ where $f(x)=x^2$, describe the transformations applied to $f$ to obtain $h$.
questions.answer: Shift $f$ left $3$ units (from $x+3$), then reflect the result over the $x$-axis (from the negative sign outside).

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: investment growth and doubling time

questions.q: This question has three parts. An investment fund grows according to $A(t)=A_0e^{0.045t}$, where $A_0$ is the initial amount (in dollars) and $t$ is time in years. (a) If $A_0=8000$ dollars, find $A(10)$ to the nearest dollar. (b) Find the time $t$, to the nearest tenth of a year, for the investment to double. (c) Solve for $t$ in terms of $A$ and $A_0$ — that is, find the inverse function $t(A)$.
questions.answer: (a) $A(10)=8000e^{0.45}\approx8000(1.5683)\approx12546$ dollars. (b) Doubling requires $e^{0.045t}=2\Rightarrow0.045t=\ln2\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln2}{0.045}\approx15.4$ years. (c) From $A=A_0e^{rt}$: $\dfrac{A}{A_0}=e^{rt}\Rightarrow\ln\left(\dfrac{A}{A_0}\right)=rt\Rightarrow t(A)=\dfrac{1}{0.045}\ln\left(\dfrac{A}{A_0}\right)$.
